name: Thachanadan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2015. Ethnologue, 18th ed.: Thachanadan [thn] (Internet Archive copy 2016).
sources.note: Entry has no Typology/phonology field; population, location, lexical similarity, language use only.

sources.citation: Ravi Sankar S. Nair 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13:7 (July 2013), 59 pp.
sources.note: No Thachanadan chapter; 'Tachanatu Muppan' speech mentioned only in the Malamuthan chapter (p. 36) for the word-initial v > m change. No stress statement for any language; preface notes Somasekharan Nair first recorded 'Tachanadu Mooppan' speech.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority 2006. Change Request 2006-029: create [thn] Thachanadan (B. Waugh, SIL), citing Jose Mathew et al. 2004, Selected Tribes and Castes of Wayanad, Kerala: A sociolinguistic study (unpublished NLCI report).
sources.note: Lexical-similarity percentages only (60-64% Malayalam, 66-72% Mullu Kurumba); nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1996. Thachanadan Mooppan Language. In: T. Madhava Menon (ed.), The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II, pp. 327-328. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. (preceded by the ethnographic entry 'Thachanadan Mooppan' by M. Sasikumar, pp. 324-327)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Phonology' section (p. 327-328) covers final-vowel + y glide + -u (eli > eliyu), a > o before final m (alam > ayom), NC clusters > geminate voiced stops (inci > ijji), a dental lateral, and v > m (vattam > mattam); then pronouns, number, case, tense, kinship terms. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the article.
sources.venue: The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. 1987. Survey of the tribal speech forms of Kerala: some comments on the questionnaires. International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XVI(1) (January 1987): c. 144-150.
sources.note: Methodological paper; Thachanadan cited only for a four-way lexical distinction for 'louse'. Nothing on phonology or stress.
sources.venue: International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics XVI(1) (January 1987): c. 144-150

sources.citation: International Journal of Dravidian Linguistics vol. 12 (1983): list of Kerala tribes ('Thachanadan (Wynad)') in a survey-planning article.
sources.note: Name appears only in a list of tribes; no linguistic data.

sources.citation: Malayalam Wikipedia, 'തച്ചനാടൻ മൂപ്പൻ' (Thachanadan Mooppan); English Wikipedia 'Thachanadan language'.
sources.note: Ml-wiki says only that they speak an archaic form of Malayalam; en-wiki stub cites Ethnologue 18. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Dravidian Encyclopaedia, Vol. III: Language and Literature (ISDL, Thiruvananthapuram, 1997/2010), entry on Tachanadan/Thachanadan Muppan speech (Ravi Sankar S. Nair states his tribal-language sketches were used for this volume).

sources.note: The primary field description by the only linguist who worked on Thachanadan; cited as the source of the 1996 encyclopedia article, which is a 2-page condensation. If any statement on stress/accent exists for this language it is most likely here (Malayalam-medium journal article, probably 10-20 pp.).

sources.citation: Jose Mathew, Binny Abraham et al. 2004. Selected Tribes and Castes of Wayanad, Kerala: A sociolinguistic study. Unpublished survey report, NLCI / IICCC, Bangalore (basis of ISO 639-3 CR 2006-029 and Ethnologue entry).

sources.note: Only other first-hand linguistic data on Thachanadan (210-item wordlists with phonetic transcription); SIL-style survey reports occasionally note stress in the transcription conventions. Might be obtainable from SIL/NLCI on request.

sources.citation: Somasekharan Nair, P. (Dept. of Malayalam Lexicon) 1992. Kinship Terminology and the Social Structure of the Tribals of Kerala. Mimeographed project report, University of Kerala, Thiruvananthapuram; and any University of Kerala Dept. of Linguistics M.A. dissertation on Tachanadan/Thachanadan Muppan speech (Ravi Sankar Nair 2013 preface says such student field studies exist but are unknown outside the department).
